basis: eBay listings and settled auctions by trading card game
note: Three different kinds of number live here. endingToday is how many auctions eBay says close within 24 hours -- a real count, not a sample -- while ended/sold are the ones we actually re-read after close, which is a small fraction of that. ended, sold, sellThrough, amount, medPrice and priceN cover the daily sample only -- the auctions ending soonest when that day's snapshot was taken, including the ones already being watched as extras at that moment (before 2026-10-15 those are restored from the watch-list history as a lower bound, so a few of the earliest-closing sample auctions may still sit with the extras); extraEnded, extraSold and extraAmount are the other extra auctions read with leftover quota, picked at other hours, kept apart and never mixed into the rates. On a daily row, sampleWatched is how many auctions were in that day's sample (null when not recorded) and sampleSettled how many of them were read back after close, counted by the day the sample was picked rather than the day it closed. live and liveFixed are how many listings were open when we looked, so a week is the AVERAGE of its days -- adding them would count the same listing every day it stayed up. ended, sold and amount are things that happened inside the period, so a week is the SUM. Sell-through is left null under 20 settled auctions and medPrice under 5, because a rate built on a handful of listings is noise. None of this is the size of a game's market: eBay is one channel, fixed-price listings are counted but we cannot see whether they sold, and shipping is excluded. What it is good for is comparing games with each other, since every game is measured the same way. offHour marks a day whose snapshot -- and so its settled sample, the auctions ending soonest at that moment -- was taken outside 00:00-04:00 UTC; offHourDays counts those days in a week or month, and the sums still include them.
